name: regolet-ssh-mcp

tools.name: ssh_connect
tools.description: Connect to a remote SSH server using password authentication. Optionally connect through a jump host (bastion server). Returns a connectionId for use with other tools.

host.description: Hostname or IP address of the target server

password.description: SSH password. Optional for blank-password OpenWrt routers or key-based default logins.

host.description: Jump host hostname or IP address

jumpHost.description: Optional jump/bastion host to tunnel through. Provide {host, username, password?, port?}

tools.name: ssh_disconnect
tools.description: Disconnect from a remote SSH server. If connectionId is omitted, disconnects the default (most recently used) connection.

connectionId.description: The connection ID to disconnect. Omit to disconnect the default connection.

tools.name: ssh_execute
tools.description: Execute a shell command on a remote SSH server. Returns stdout, stderr, and exit code. Commands are executed in a new shell session — use "&&" or ";" to chain commands (e.g., "cd /etc && cat hosts"). For long-running commands, increase the timeout.

command.description: The shell command to execute on the remote server

connectionId.description: Connection ID to use. Omit to use the default connection.

timeout.description: Command timeout in milliseconds (default: 30000 = 30 seconds). Increase for long-running commands.

tools.name: ssh_upload
tools.description: Upload/write text content to a file on the remote server via SFTP. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. For binary files, use ssh_execute with base64 encoding instead.

remotePath.description: Absolute path on the remote server where the file should be written (e.g., "/tmp/script.sh")

content.description: The text content to write to the file

connectionId.description: Connection ID to use. Omit to use the default connection.

tools.name: ssh_download
tools.description: Download/read text content from a file on the remote server via SFTP. Returns the file content as a string. Best for text files — for binary files, use ssh_execute with base64/cat instead.

remotePath.description: Absolute path of the file to read on the remote server (e.g., "/etc/nginx/nginx.conf")

connectionId.description: Connection ID to use. Omit to use the default connection.

tools.name: ssh_list_dir
tools.description: List the contents of a directory on the remote server via SFTP. Returns file names, types (file/directory/symlink), sizes, permissions, and modification dates. Directories are listed first, sorted alphabetically.

remotePath.description: Absolute path of the directory to list (default: "/")

connectionId.description: Connection ID to use. Omit to use the default connection.

tools.name: ssh_status
tools.description: Check the status of SSH connections. If connectionId is provided, shows status for that specific connection. Otherwise, shows status for all active connections.

connectionId.description: Specific connection ID to check. Omit to see all connections.

tools.name: ssh_list_connections
tools.description: List all active SSH connections with their IDs, hosts, and connection timestamps.

tools.name: ssh_list_hosts
tools.description: List all available SSH hosts (from encrypted database and/or environment variables). Shows host name, address, username, description, and tags — never passwords. Use ssh_connect_host to connect by name.

tools.name: ssh_find_host
tools.description: Search for a host by keyword. Searches across host name, hostname/IP, description, and tags. Use this to find the right server for a task (e.g., search "database" to find DB servers, "openwrt" to find routers).

query.description: Search keyword to match against host name, description, address, or tags

tools.name: ssh_connect_host
tools.description: Connect to a saved SSH host by its name. No credentials needed in the conversation — credentials are loaded from the encrypted database or environment. Use ssh_list_hosts first to see available hosts.

name.description: The name/alias of the host to connect to (e.g., "router", "web-server")

tools.name: ssh_add_host
tools.description: Save a host to the encrypted database (~/.regolet-ssh/hosts.enc). The password is encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM — never stored in plain text. Optionally specify a jump host (bastion) for tunneled connections. The host becomes immediately available for ssh_connect_host.

password.description: SSH password (will be encrypted at rest). Optional for blank-password targets.

description.description: What this server does (helps AI pick the right host)

jumpHost.description: Optional jump/bastion host for tunneled connections

tools.name: ssh_remove_host
tools.description: Remove a host from the encrypted database. This does not disconnect any active SSH connection — just removes the saved credentials.

name.description: The name of the host to remove from the database

tools.name: ssh_pull_to_disk
tools.description: Download a remote file or entire directory directly to your local machines disk. Uses raw tar streams to bypass SFTP limitations (e.g. OpenWrt) and prevents large files from flooding the AI context memory.

remotePath.description: Absolute path of the file or directory to pull from the remote server (e.g., "/etc/config")

localPath.description: Absolute path of the local destiny directory where files will be written (e.g., "C:/backups/router")

connectionId.description: Connection ID to use. Omit to use the default connection.

tools.name: ssh_push_from_disk
tools.description: Upload a local file or entire directory directly to the remote server. Uses raw tar streams to bypass SFTP limitations. Ideal for bulk copying nested folders.

localPath.description: Absolute path of the local file or directory to push (e.g., "C:/backups/router/config")

remotePath.description: Absolute path of the target directory on the remote server (e.g., "/etc")

connectionId.description: Connection ID to use. Omit to use the default connection.
